subject: Difficulty reading in bismark sam alignment files into MethylKit

messages.author: 6e7850188b207822
messages.subject: Difficulty reading in bismark sam alignment files into MethylKit
parts:
Hi,

Apologies I am quite inexperienced with bioinformatics...

I would like to do some preliminary data exploration on my single-end RRBS data and MethylKit seems the ideal program for doing this.

I have aligned reads for each individual against a reference genome using Bismark and have extracted methylation calls for each aligned C nucleotide. However, I very confused as to the best way to import my data into R for analysis in MethylKit.

Is the most convenient format for doing this the sam file produced by the Bismark alignment?

If so, do I still need to sort the sam file by chromosome and read position? It is suggested to use the sort command, however there is very little available information that I could find on the best way to do this. Someone on this forum suggested the following command:

"sort -snk3 -k4 Sample_bismark_bt2_pe.sam > sorted_Sample_bismark_bt2_pe.sam" - would this work?

I also read in the same forum query that chromosomes/scaffolds have to start with "Chr"- Is this still the case?

My aligned sam file format looks like this:

NB501345:34:HY7G5BGXY:2:13312:21020:9410_1:N:0:GAGGCG   0       000000F|quiver  8439 ......

Would I need to insert "Chr" into every line, making it something like Chr000000F|quiver in the above example?

What would be the best tool for doing this conversion on a sam file of several Gbs?

Many thanks for any help you can give

Alan

messages.author: 5476946a951cd54c
messages.subject: Re: Difficulty reading in bismark sam alignment files into MethylKit
parts:
I think I can answer my own question (hopefully this will be of help to other dabblers like me)

Basically I took the aligned sam output from Bismark (v0.17.0) and first removed the header:

$ grep -v '^@' test.sam > test.noheader.sam

Then I sorted the resulting sam file by chromosome and read start position

$  sort -sn -k3,3 -k4,4 test.noheader.sam > test.sorted.sam

I then prepended 'Chr' onto the Chromosome/Scaffold name

$  awk 'BEGIN { OFS = "\t" } { $03 = "Chr" $03; print }' test.sorted.sam > test.Chr_sorted.sam

The final resulting sam file has the following file format and appears to successfully import into MethylKit using the processBismarkAln() command:

NB501345:33:HWMGLBGXY:1:11101:1621:9879_1:N:0:TACAGC    0    Chr000000F|quiver    1276    34    75M    *    0    0    CGGTGATATGGGGTTTTTAGGGATTAGTAAAGTGTTTTATAAATATAGGTTATTTATTAATTTAGTAGATGAAGT    AA/AAEEEEEEAEAEA/AEAEEEEEEEEAEEEEEEAEEEAEEEEEEEAEE/EEEEEEE/EEEEEEEEEE/EAEAE    NM:i:16    MD:Z:14C0C1C5C8C1C4C5C3C0C5C0C4C2C3C4C0    XM:Z:Z.............hh.x.....h........z.h....h.....x...hh.....hh....x..x...z....x    XR:Z:CT    XG:Z:CT

Hope that helps
